resources.string: VettID keeps your messages, connections and most important secrets in a vault that only you can open.
Your keys stay on this phone and in your vault\'s sealed enclave.
Enter the email address of your VettID account. We will email you a sign-in link.
If %1$s belongs to a VettID account, a sign-in link is on its way. Open it on this phone. It works once, for 15 minutes.
That is not a VettID sign-in link.
You are signing in as %1$s. Only continue if you asked for this link.
This link is not valid any more. Ask for a new one.
Your account asks for its sign-in PIN, the one you set on the account site. It is not your vault PIN.
That account PIN is not correct.
Your account is registered. To get a vault, become a member by accepting the membership terms on the account site.
The membership terms have changed. Accept the current terms on the account site to keep using your vault.
I have accepted them, check again
Your account already has a vault
A vault has exactly one app, which holds its credential. Another phone is that app.
Move VettID with a direct transfer from that phone. It needs your PIN and credential password, and no waiting.
Start a recovery on the account site. After 24 hours this phone can take over with your PIN and password, and the old app is removed.
Set up a new vault anyway
Your PIN unlocks your vault. Only your vault\'s sealed enclave ever checks it, and wrong guesses are slowed down. Use at least 6 digits; avoid dates and simple patterns.
The PINs do not match. Try again.
It protects your Protean Credential and your critical items, and VettID asks for it at every critical action. Make it different from your PIN. Nobody, VettID included, can reset it.
Choose where your credential lives. You can change this later in Credential.
Your vault keeps a copy sealed to it and to your password. If you lose this phone, a recovery restores your credential and critical items.
Your credential lives only on this phone. No copy exists anywhere else.
Losing this phone loses your credential

With the backup off, losing or resetting this phone loses your credential and every critical item permanently. A recovery can then only reset the credential, destroying your critical items, or delete the vault.
I understand that losing this phone loses my credential and critical items
This takes a moment. Keep VettID open.
Verifying the vault service and this phone
Your vault is enrolled, this phone holds its credential, and only your PIN opens it.
Invite someone with a QR code or a link, compare the safety code, and start messaging. Connections arrive in the next update.
Your vault now runs release %1$d (fingerprint %2$s); this phone last used release %3$d. Another of your devices approved this update. Continue only if you expected it.
Your vault is served by release %1$d, older than release %2$d that this phone last used. VettID will not send your PIN to it.
It ends on %1$s. Update to keep your vault working.
Update to the newest release to keep your vault working.
Your vault runs release %1$d. Release %2$d (fingerprint %3$s) is available. Anyone can rebuild it and compare the fingerprint.
Approve the update with this unlock
Too many wrong PINs. Try again in %1$s.

Someone started a recovery of this vault from the account site, so it is locked for this phone. If that was you on a new phone, let it finish there. If it was not you, cancel it now: unlocking here with your PIN cancels the recovery.
Your vault\'s state is older than expected
The vault\'s stored state is older than state this phone has already seen. Someone may have restored an old copy. Contact VettID support before you continue.
The update was refused (%1$s). Your vault stayed on its current release.
Your vault did not recognise this phone. It may have been replaced by a recovery or a transfer.
Use your fingerprint, face or screen lock to open VettID.
